records.name: Mount Carleton Fire Tower
records.agency: Province of New Brunswick (Mount Carleton Provincial Park)

extra.status_note: Log cabin lookout 1923; replaced 1939 by a frame cupola cabin (annual report via weebly); not staffed after 1968 (park sign via Hiking NB). Summit tower and cabin still stand per Hiking NB and Highpoints of Canada. NHLR CAN 23, NB 2 (registered 2026-06-01).
extra.access_text: Summit of New Brunswick's highest peak, inside Mount Carleton Provincial Park; 9.3 km Mount Carleton Trail loop (Hiking NB); park entrance fee.

records.name: Barr Settlement
records.agency: Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources

extra.status_note: NHLR CAN 6, NS 1 (registered 1998-08-15): 100 ft steel tower with fibreglass cab, second lookout in the province. Nova Scotia DNR closed its tower network in 2013 and, per CBC (2025), decommissioned and dismantled the towers in 2015; this site is in Marscan's 2009 list of 33 operating DNR towers. Individual removal date not confirmed unless stated.

records.name: New Yarmouth Fire Tower
records.agency: Minas Basin Pulp & Paper (1940s); Nova Scotia Department of Natural Resources (later)

extra.status_note: Wikipedia (New Yarmouth): built by Minas Basin Pulp and Paper in the 1940s, taken over by the DNR, staffed seasonally until 2012 (a longtime observer retired 1999), closed 2013 and demolished June 2015. In Cape Chignecto Provincial Park. An RCAF radar-and-fire-tower combination proposed there in 1960 was never built.

records.name: Tour d'observation du mont du Général-Allard (Valcartier)
records.agency: Canadian Forces Base Valcartier (Department of National Defence)

extra.status_note: SOPFEU blog: the last tower in use in Quebec was on the Valcartier base atop Mont Général Allard (60 ft), used until 1981. OSM node 11532690714 (emergency=fire_lookout, unnamed) is 90 m from CGNDB "Mont du Général-Allard". Whether it stands now is not stated.
extra.access_text: Inside the Valcartier military base; aircraft detection patrols were not allowed there, so a tower stayed in use.
extra.confidence: OSM point + CGNDB summit + SOPFEU text agree on the place

records.name: Tour de la Montagne du Diable
records.agency: Lower Ottawa Forest Protective Association (1915); James Maclaren Company (about 1930)

extra.status_note: Canadian Forestry Journal (June 1915, via weebly): 42-foot lookout tower and ranger camp erected on the highest peak of Devil's Mountain, Robertson township. La Presse touristique: a Maclaren tower was installed about 1930; a new "Tour du Garde-Feu" was inaugurated at the Parc régional de la Montagne du Diable as a tribute. BAnQ holds a 192-? photo file of the Devil Mountain tower.

records.name: Tour du lac Matapédia
records.agency: Fenderson / timber company (J.N.O. Fenderson per the Maniwaki interpretation text)

extra.status_note: Said to be the first fire-detection tower on Quebec soil: inaugurated 1910 south of Lac Matapédia, 518 m elevation (SOPFEU; Ville de Maniwaki). The Ottawa Journal of 17 Aug 1912 (via weebly) describes a 50-foot steel tower on a rise about 2,300 ft above sea level; the two elevations differ.

records.name: Tour n° 5 du lac Carotte
records.agency: St. Maurice Forest Protective Association

aliases: Tour no 5 (St. Maurice Forest Protective Association)
extra.status_note: SHFQ/AFFPAN panel: ordered 19 Nov 1923, received 15 Jan 1924, erected Feb-Mar 1924; 80-foot steel tower, open wooden cab, model no. 1395 by Goold, Shapley & Muir (Brantford, ON); one of 75 new SMFPA towers of 1923-24; on the mountain at lac Carotte in the Saint-Zénon pourvoirie sector. Current state not stated.

records.name: Tour à feu de Luskville
records.agency: Ministère des Forêts, de la Faune et des Parcs (NHLR); National Capital Commission cooperating (Gatineau Park)

aliases: Tour à feu (Parc de la Gatineau)
extra.status_note: NHLR CAN 12, QC 2 (registered 2022-12-25): wood cab on steel supports, built 1940, weathered. RPCQ inventory fiche 173551 (Pontiac) says built 1944 by the Quebec natural-resources ministry, lost its fire role in 1978, recycled since the 2000s as a radio communications tower with a wind turbine and solar panels (2008). Year conflict 1940 vs 1944. OSM node 1170985916 and the RPCQ position agree within 300 m.
extra.access_text: Gatineau Park, top of the Eardley Escarpment above Luskville Falls; RPCQ: reached by a trail from chemin Ridge south of Lac Mousseau.

extra.status_note: Tourisme Mégantic lists "the fire tower" among the points of interest of the Piopolis heritage circuit; nothing else checked.

records.agency: Municipalité d'Amherst (owner; restored 1997)

extra.status_note: NHLR CAN 11, QC 1 (registered 2022-12-25); RPCQ fiche 196596 (Inventaire MRC des Laurentides 2013) agrees on position (46 1' 16.17" N, 74 46' 48.64" W) and year (1930). CGNDB "Montagne de la Tour" in Amherst sits on the same spot.
extra.access_text: Trail from chemin Saint-Louis (about 1.5 km); NHLR says climbing the tower is forbidden.

records.name: Tour à feu du lac des Rapides (Sept-Îles)

extra.status_note: Les Sentiers de la Côte describes a 10-12 km trail to the "ancienne tour à feu du lac des Rapides" near Sept-Îles. Possibly the LFPA "Lac Rapide"/"Rapide" tower (Clarke City division), not confirmed.

records.name: Tour à feu du mont Morissette
records.agency: Parc régional du Mont-Morissette (municipality of Blue Sea), per Géo Plein Air

extra.status_note: RPCQ inventory fiche 173368 (Blue Sea): steel-framed tower with stair, built about 1945, chemin de la Tour. Géo Plein Air describes an authentic steel fire tower next to a new 18 m observation tower at the summit of mont Morissette, one of the few survivors in the Vallée-de-la-Gatineau. RPCQ position is 250 m from the CGNDB summit "Mont Morisette".
extra.access_text: Regional park trail (2.1 km short route) with interpretive panels at the summit.
extra.confidence: RPCQ coordinates (seconds-level); merge with the weebly entry rests on the place name
